## Astra Chemistry — New obstruction: authenticating a donor is not the same as selecting the current instruction

The previous two-key PNA model assumes that candidate donors compete for one active recognition site. Its favourable long-programme calculations are valid under that assumption, but they do not establish that a long DNA template exposes only one site to donor binding.

If downstream addresses can also bind their matching donors, those donors may survive the same wash and become chemically active before the growing peptide reaches them.

This is a fundamental distinction:

- Identity authentication: Is this donor correctly matched to this DNA address?
- Instruction authentication: Is this address the next one the growing molecule must execute?

A donor can pass the first test and fail the second.

The experimental comparator is substantial. Meng and colleagues' autonomous DNA assembler already demonstrated programmed covalent synthesis, while the later mechanism proposed by Bath and Turberfield explicitly addresses chemical-reaction-dependent instruction progression. Neither establishes the independent, retryable peptide synthesis operation sought here. 

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://www.nature.com\&sz=32)

Nature Chemistry+1



The new target is therefore to make donor authentication depend jointly on its DNA address and the position of the chemically growing product, without allowing that recognition event itself to count as a successful peptide bond.

## Exact result: future-address exposure creates a quadratic burden

I extended the previous donor-loading model to include every unused downstream address and all retries after missed incorporation.

Let \\(q\\) be the probability an unused address retains an activatable donor after washing, and \\(\chi\\) the probability that such a retained donor causes a fatal incorrect reaction during one activation pulse. Suppose the current intended reaction succeeds with probability \\(p\\), makes an irreversible wrong bond with probability \\(w\\), and the parent suffers independent damage with probability \\(\delta\\).

For \\(L\\) required incorporations, the exact eventual all-correct probability is

\\[ \boxed{ F_L=\prod\_{m=0}^{L-1} \frac{p(1-\delta)(1-q\chi)^m} {1-(1-p-w)(1-\delta)(1-q\chi)^m}. } \\]

CHEMICAL AUTHENTICATION AND ESCAPE
For rates B2->B1=2u, B1->B2=v, B1->U=u, U->B1=b, U->E=c, the backward equations give T_single=(b+c)/(u c)+1/c for a SINGLE-contact architecture without B1->B2. In the two-contact architecture T2=T_single+1/(2u)+v(b+c)/(2u²c). This comparison assumes u,c>0, finite nonnegative b,v, memoryless fixed rates and actual escape E. The same B1 label across architectures is not the same dynamics; without physical removal (c=0) these finite formulas do not apply. Long residence does not authenticate the next instruction or prove a covalent amide.
At a stage with m unused addresses, supplied independent fresh retention/side-reaction survival a_m=(1-delta)(1-q chi)^m gives success p*a_m and retry (1-p-w)*a_m. Geometric summation yields p*a_m/[1-(1-p-w)*a_m], and multiplying stages gives the native product. It requires legitimate probabilities and retry probability<1. To first order about w=delta=qchi=0, the downstream derivative of -logF is L(L-1)/(2p). This scaling is conditional on fresh independent nonlocal fatal hazards; distance-decaying interactions and memory change the model. It is not a chemical no-go.
A second recognition factor identical for wrong and correct candidates multiplies both equilibrium association weights equally and leaves their ratio unchanged. A slow generic second key can retain wrong donors; exact finite kinetic numbers are source-only absent the programmes. Donor identity, current instruction identity, product-bond fate and cleanup/advancement are different interfaces. A product-attached frontier key plus address is a PROPOSED construction with unresolved register, old handles, temporary thioesters, stalled parents, sink, fuel, compatibility and permanent wrong-bond obligations, not an accepted working relay. No protocol or new measured chemistry is acquired here.
